label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 5 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: poison-message
case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer that retries unreadable messages forever (BAD_EVENTS=retry), then one unreadable event from the provider (a payment.updated with its amount as a decimal string): the ledger consumer is stuck on it, and books nothing behind it.
case.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to dead-lettering: the poison goes to the dead-letter topic, the backlog drains, and the money check passes again

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 159.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 06:03:15 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. Since then it has been stuck on one event, provider-events partition 1 offset 113, which the ledger refuses with 'amount must be positive integer cents'. It retries that same message every 15 s (attempt 9 at 06:04:17) and books nothing behind it, so ledger lag grows on all three partitions. The money check therefore cannot settle up to its cutoff, and BooksBehindProvider fires. payment-confirmer is deployed with BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter and has zero lag, so only the ledger path is blocked. The bad amount in the event is not explained: it may come from the provider payload or from payments-api, and no call here checked that. I also have not seen the ledger-consumer's previous settings, only that it was recreated with retry.

evidence.shows: Total consumer lag went from 0 to 4 to 216 in the last two minutes, so the alert's symptom is real.
Only the ledger consumer's lag is growing, on partitions 0, 1 and 2 (about 72 each). payment-confirmer is at 0 on every partition.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 06:03:15 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry, just as lag began. payment-confirmer uses BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.

ledger-consumer logs 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/1@113, with error 'amount must be positive integer cents'. Attempts 3 to 9 are logged with the same error, and the retry delay is now 15 s.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before the 06:03:15 deploy. This should stop the infinite retry on the bad event, so the consumer moves past it and catches up. Afterwards, check that the event at provider-events/1@113 went to the dead letters and not into the ledger. Then find why its amount is not positive integer cents, in the provider payload or in payments-api. Re-run money_check once the lag is 0.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The ledger-consumer container is recreated and pauses briefly while it restarts, so ledger booking stops for that time; payments, refunds and payment-confirmer are not affected. A rollback repairs nothing already booked. If the previous settings also fail on this event, or if the bad event is dropped without being dead-lettered, a ledger entry could be missing and the money check would still flag it.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy ledger-consumer with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry (the settings shown in c3). Then rewind or skip offset 113 on partition 1 by hand and re-run money_check.
